test_title: SSC GD Constable Previous Year Paper (Held on: 8th December 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: The compound interest on a sum of ₹8,400 in 3 years at a certain rate percent per annum is ₹6115.20, interest being compounded annually. What will be the difference in (₹) between compound interest on the same sum at the same rate for 1{1 over 2} years, when the interest is compounded half yearly and the simple interest on the same sum for same rate and for the same period?
solution:
**Given:**

Principal = Rs. 8400, Time Period = 3 years

Compound Interest = Rs. 6115.20

**Formula used:**

Compound Interest = P × [1 + (R/100)]ⁿ - P

Simple Interest = [P × R × T]/100

Where P = Principal, R = Rate of interest, n = Time in years

**Calculation:**

According to the Question,

Compound Interest = P × [1 + (R/100)]n - P

⇒ 6115.20 = 8400 × (1 + R/100)³ - 8400

⇒ 6115.20 + 8400 = 8400[((100 + R)/100)³]

⇒ 14515.20/8400 = [(100 + R)/100]³

⇒ 1728/1000 = [(100 + R)/100]3 

⇒ [(100 + R)/100] = (1728/1000)¹/³

⇒ [(100 + R)/100] = 12/10

⇒ R = 20%

Compound interest for 1{1 over 2} years, when compounded half-yearly

∴ R = 20/2 = 10%, and T = 3 years

Compound Interest = P × [1 + (R/100)]n - P

⇒ 8400 × [(100 + 10%)/100]³ - 8400

⇒ 8400[(110/100)³ - 1]

⇒ 8400 × 331/1000 = 2780.4

Simple Interest on the same sum for the same rate and time,

⇒ Simple Interest = [P × R × T]/100

⇒ [8400 × 20 × (3/2)]/100 = 2520

The required difference = 2780.4 - 2520 = 260.4

**∴ Hence the required difference is ₹ 260.4**
